Experienced Legal Assistant Commercial Property
Salary: £27,000 - £30,000 DOE
Location: Northampton

SJC Legal is currently working with a well-established and highly regarded law firm looking to recruit an experienced Legal Assistant to join its growing Commercial Property team in Northampton.

This is an excellent opportunity for an established Legal Assistant or Legal Secretary who enjoys working within a busy property department and is looking for a long-term legal support position. You will work closely with experienced Commercial Property fee earners, providing essential administrative and transactional support and playing an important role in the smooth running of the department.

The Benefits
- Competitive salary depending on experience
- Full-time, permanent position
- Opportunity to join an established and expanding Commercial Property team
- Work directly alongside experienced Commercial Property fee earners
- Exposure to a broad range of commercial property transactions
- Established and highly regarded regional law firm
- Supportive and collaborative working environment
- Varied and responsible legal support position

The Role
- Provide day-to-day administrative and legal support to Commercial Property fee earners
- Assist with the progression of commercial property transactions
- Submit online property searches
- Prepare and submit Land Registry applications

For a confidential discussion regarding this opportunity, or to discuss other legal support and Commercial Property positions currently available, please contact Alex Wilcock, Legal Recruitment Consultant at SJC Legal.

title: Accounts Assistant
company: Macildowie Recruitment and Retention - Agency - Permanent
description:
Job Description

Accounts Assistant

This is an excellent opportunity for an Accounts Assistant to join the Finance team of an established venue in a varied, all-round role. Working as part of a close-knit Finance team, you'll support a range of day-to-day accounting activities including invoice processing, account queries, bank reconciliations and general finance administration.

The business is looking to strengthen the Finance function as it continues to develop, providing additional capacity and support across the team. The role would suit someone with a broad understanding of transactional finance who is happy to work across different areas and provide support where required.

About the Role

As an Accounts Assistant, you'll join a Finance team currently consisting of 3 people. The team is moving towards clearer ownership of different areas, while continuing to provide cover and support across the wider Finance function.

Your responsibilities will include processing invoices, dealing with invoice and account queries, completing bank reconciliations and supporting the team with general finance administration.

The role offers good variety, with the opportunity to gain exposure across different areas of Finance rather than being focused solely on one transactional process. While there will be clearer ownership within the team, a broad finance skill set and willingness to support colleagues will be important.

This is a fully office-based position in Daventry, working Monday to Friday, 9am-5pm.

Key Responsibilities
- Process invoices accurately and efficiently.
- Deal with invoice and account queries from internal and external contacts.
- Complete bank reconciliations and assist with maintaining accurate financial records.
- Provide general finance administration and day-to-day support to the Finance team.
- Support different areas of transactional Finance as required.
- Provide cover and assistance to colleagues across the Finance function.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial information.
- Assist with the smooth running of day-to-day Finance processes.
- Work collaboratively with the wider Finance team to ensure workloads are managed effectively.
- Take ownership of allocated responsibilities while remaining flexible to support the wider team.

Key Requirements
- Previous experience within an Accounts Assistant, Finance Assistant or similar transactional Finance role.
- Good understanding of general accounting and Finance processes.
- Experience processing invoices and dealing with account queries.
- Experience completing bank reconciliations is desirable.
- Good attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Good organisational and time management skills.
- Confident communicator with the ability to work effectively with colleagues and other contacts.
- Comfortable working across a varied Finance role rather than being restricted to one area.
- Flexible and willing to provide support across the Finance team when required.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Excel.
- Reliable, proactive and able to work as part of a small team.
- Willingness to learn and develop within a broader Finance environment.

If you're interested in this role, please apply with your most recent CV as soon as possible.
Interviews will be taking place at the start of October.

title: Part-time Payroll Administrator
description:
Part-Time Payroll Administrator

£30,000 - £35,000 pro rata

Role based in Wellingborough

Are you an experienced Payroll Administrator looking for a flexible part-time role where you can take ownership of payroll while supporting the wider HR function of a successful SME?

Cole Connections are recruiting for a Part-Time HR / Payroll Administrator to join a growing business in Wellingborough on a 12-month fixed-term contract, with the potential for the position to become permanent.

This role offers between 16 and 24 hours per week, with flexibility around how those hours are worked. Due to payroll deadlines, some flexibility to work additional hours during busier periods is required, and Mondays are essential.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Processing the monthly payroll for approximately 100 employees using Moorepay
- Ensuring payroll is completed accurately and within required deadlines
- Generating payroll and wage reports
- Producing absence reports and maintaining absence records
- Supporting absence monitoring and administration activities
- Preparing employment contracts and associated documentation
- Maintaining employee records and HR files
- Supporting onboarding and employee administration processes
- Ensuring confidentiality and accuracy across all payroll and HR activities

The ideal candidate will have:
- Previous experience processing payroll from start to finish with minimal supervision
- The ability to quickly learn and confidently use payroll software - the system you will use is Moorepay so if you have used this before that would be amazing

- Experience producing payroll, wage and absence reports

- Excellent organisational and time management skills
- The ability to manage confidential information professionally

If you have proven payroll experience and are looking for a flexible role within a friendly SME environment, we would be delighted to hear from you.

title: Credit Controller
company: Macildowie Recruitment and Retention - Agency - Permanent
description:
Credit Controller

Join a growing Credit Control team within an established and successful business, where you'll play an important role in supporting customers, resolving outstanding debt and managing credit risk. Following the implementation of a new business-wide system, the Credit Control function has expanded, creating an exciting opportunity for proactive Credit Controllers to join the team on a permanent basis.

About the Role

As a Credit Controller, you'll work closely with both internal teams and external customers to ensure outstanding debts are collected efficiently and invoice queries are resolved promptly. You'll also review credit limits in line with customer spend and risk, identify recurring issues and help implement effective solutions.

You'll be joining a highly supportive and collaborative Finance team, where colleagues work together to achieve shared goals and support one another through periods of change and increased activity.

Key Responsibilities
- Ensure outstanding debts are collected promptly when they fall due.
- Investigate and resolve invoice queries by liaising with internal teams and customers.
- Ensure appropriate resolutions are documented accurately.
- Identify and escalate high-risk customer accounts to management.
- Review accounts that have exceeded agreed credit limits and liaise with senior colleagues where appropriate.
- Identify recurring issues and disputes, recommend solutions and support their implementation.
- Maintain strong relationships with customers while providing a high standard of service.

Key Requirements
- Previous experience working within a Credit Control or Sales Ledger role.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Word.
- Strong time management, planning and organisational skills.
- Proactive and solutions-focused approach to problem-solving.
- Enthusiastic team player with a willingness to support colleagues.
- A customer-focused approach, with strong integrity and attention to detail.

What's on Offer
- Permanent opportunity within a supportive and collaborative Finance team.
- Bonus opportunity.
- Discounts, savings and cashback across numerous retailers.
- Life assurance.
- Enhanced family-friendly policies, including maternity, paternity and additional annual leave.
- Mental Health First Aiders and Employee Assistance Programme.
- Comprehensive induction and ongoing development opportunities.
- Financial education and access to financial support.
- Inclusive working environment where everyone is encouraged to be themselves.
- Opportunity to join a business investing in its people and long-term growth.

title: Group Accounts Assistant
description:
Group Accounts Assistant

Location: Remote (preferred locations Northamptonshire/ Milton Keynes)

Hours: 25 hours per week (negotiable)

Salary: £30,000 pa, depending on experience

Join a growing team making a real impact

At Impact HR, and across our associated group companies, we are continuing to scale our operations and support to our client base.

To support this growth, we are recruiting for a Group Accounts Assistant who will be responsible for overseeing the day-to-day bookeeping and accounting of multiple companies within the business to support the Group Management Accountant.

This is a part-time role suited to a developing accounting professional who enjoys working in a growing SME environment and has the organisational skills to manage multiple entities. This role will progress bookkeeping skills with the complexity of supporting multiple companies within the group, with opportunities for the right candidate to develop further accounting skills.

Why this role matters

As the business grows, maintaining accuracy within Accounts Payable and Accounts Recievable of our various companies becomes increasingly important.

This role ensures the business maintains:
- Timely processing of Payable invoices
- Accurate delivery of Sales invoicing
- Monitoring of Aging debtors
- Responding to customer queries in a timely and professional manner

The Group Accounts Assistant will play an important role in supporting business leaders by ensuring the fundamentals of bookkeeping are accurate across the companies in their remit.

What you will be doing

You will be responsible for Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable of 3 companies, reporting to the Group Management Accountant.

This role oversees all core bookkeeping elements, with opportunities for accounting tasks and professional development.

Your day-to-day will include:

Within 3 of our companies:

Accounts Payable
- Processing and approving supplier invoices
- Reconciling bank account transactions
- Monitoring the Accounts mailboxes and responding to queries
- Maintaining and reviewing the fixed asset registers

Accounts Receivable
- Raising Sales invoices for 2-3 entities
- Chasing overdue invoices and resolving client invoice queries

What Success Looks Like (First 12 Months)
- Accurate and timely processing of purchase and sales invoices
- Well maintained bookkeeping records, fixed asset registers and bank reconciliations

About You

You are a developing accounting professional who enjoys working within a growing SME environment and is comfortable managing 3 Accounts mailboxes.

You bring strong attention to detail, initiative and a professional manner. You are comfortable asking questions when unsure.

You are organised, pragmatic and able to manage your workload effectively within a part-time role.

You will likely bring:
- 1+ years experience bookkeping or accounting
- Strong grades in Mathematics
- Ideally working towards an Accounting qualification such as AAT
- Accuracy and attention to detail
- Excellent prioritising and time management skills
- Proficiency with Outlook
- Experience using Accounting systems
- A solutions-focused mindset
- Application of data protection and confidentiality

What We Offer
- Competitive salary and benefits
- Flexible working
- Supportive, values-led team culture
- Progression pathways and professional development

Ready to shape the future of hr with Impact?

We are looking for a developing accounting professional who wants to play an important role in supporting a strong accounts foundation for a growing consultancy.

This role is about more than simply bookkeeping. It is about reliability, accuracy and adding value through solid accounting fundamentals, as well as requiring mental agility and organisation skills to manage multiple companies coherently. Once comfortable with the role, there are opportunities to develop various further accounting skills.

If you enjoy working in a flexible, collaborative environment and want the opportunity to apply your accounts expertise within a growing professional services organisation, we would love to hear from you.

title: Credit Controller
description:
As a Credit Controller in the business services industry, based in Northampton, you'll play a key role in managing and maintaining the company's credit and collections processes. Your day-to-day will involve ensuring timely payments, resolving account queries, and supporting the smooth running of the accounting and finance department.

Client Details

A company in the business services industry located in Northampton.

Description

Manage and recover outstanding debt relating to fees across multiple locations.

Review and prioritise aged debt ledgers, focusing on high-value and long-outstanding accounts.

Contact responsible parties by telephone, email and letter to secure payment of overdue balances.

Investigate and resolve account queries, disputed charges and billing discrepancies that may delay payment.

Negotiate payment arrangements and repayment plans in line with company policies.

Monitor agreed payment schedules and follow up on broken arrangements.

Liaise closely with Regional Managers and Finance teams to obtain information required to support debt recovery activities.

Maintain accurate records of all communications, payment commitments and collection activity.

Escalate high-risk or non-responsive accounts through the appropriate internal and legal recovery processes.

Reconcile customer accounts and allocate payments accurately.

Profile

A successful Credit Controller should have:
- Previous experience in credit control or a similar role within accounting and finance.
- Strong numerical and analytical skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and organisational abilities.
- Confident communication skills to liaise with clients and internal teams.
- Proficiency in relevant accounting software and Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- The ability to work efficiently under pressure and meet deadlines.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and resolving account issues.

Job Offer
- Competitive salary of up to £32,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Permanent position based in Northampton.
- Opportunity to work in the business services industry.

title: Events Administrator in Motorsport
company: Katie Bard & Angela Mortimer Plc - Agency - Permanent
description:
Event Administrator

South Northamptonshire Full-time, 37.5 hours £14-£15 p/h

Do you love a busy diary, a full inbox and the buzz of a big event day? Then this might just be your dream job.

We're working with a world-class events venue in South Northamptonshire that hosts more than 40 major public events every year. They're looking for an organised, upbeat Event Administrator to join their Public Events team and keep everything running smoothly behind the scenes.

What you'll be doing

You'll be the right hand to the Head of Public Events. That means managing their diary, arranging meetings and travel, taking minutes and making sure nothing slips through the cracks.

You'll also be at the heart of the wider team. You'll run the events inbox, keep the holiday calendar in check, pull together the weekly team update and handle purchase orders, invoices and expenses.

When event season kicks in, you'll be right in the thick of it. You'll sort meal vouchers, fuel cards and minibuses, prepare event briefings and make sure every operational plan is signed off, printed and ready for event control. No two weeks are the same, and it's never boring.

What you'll bring
- At least a year's experience in an office role, ideally with some diary management
- Strong Microsoft skills, especially Outlook, Excel and PowerPoint
- A sharp eye for detail and the ability to juggle lots of projects at once
- A can-do attitude and a happy-to-jump-in-at-the-deep-end mindset
- Flexibility to work some evenings and weekends, mainly between March and December

Why you'll love it

You'll join a passionate, close-knit team that genuinely gives its all, at a venue that's famous across the country. If you want a role where you can see the results of your hard work, live and in front of thousands of fans, this is it.

title: Network HR Assistant

GXO is currently recruiting a Network HR Assistant to support our B&Q retail logistics operation. This role plays a vital part in delivering consistent, high-quality HR support across a number of unionised operational sites during a period of continuing integration and change. You'll be a trusted presence across the region, supporting managers and colleagues with the day-to-day employee lifecycle while ensuring policies, processes, and data standards are applied consistently.

This role is being offered on a full-time, permanent basis. The hours of work are 37.5 per week, 5 days per week, predominantly Monday to Friday, office hours. Some flexibility will be required, this is logistics after al!

Pay, benefits and more:

You'll be paid a salary of up to £28,500 per annum. You'll also receive 25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays), as well as the option to buy additional days so you can enjoy a positive work-life balance. Your benefits package includes flexible dental insurance plans, a company sponsored pension scheme, a 24/7 online GP service, life assurance and a fully comprehensive employee assistance programme. - Provide end-to-end HR assistance across multiple sites, including contracts, variations, starters, leavers, right-to-work checks, references, and probation tracking
- Maintain accurate HR systems and personnel files, ensuring GDPR compliance at all times
- Support employee relations activity by preparing documentation, tracking case timelines, and note-taking at meetings
- Coordinate recruitment and onboarding activities, including adverts, interviews, offers and pre-employment checks
- Produce regular HR reports including headcount, starters/leavers, absence and probation milestones
- Act as a first point of contact for HR admin queries, escalating appropriately where required

What you need to succeed at GXO:
- Proven experience in a high-volume HR assistant or coordinator role, with a good working knowledge of HR systems and employment documentation
- CIPD Level 3 is desirable, with support available for further development.
- Confidence supporting operational, unionised environments (or a strong willingness to learn)
- Strong attention to detail and pride in producing accurate, well-organised work
- Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple locations
- Clear, professional communication skills at all levels

We engineer faster, smarter, leaner supply chains.

GXO is a leading provider of cutting-edge supply chain solutions to the most successful companies in the world. We help our customers manage their goods most efficiently using our technology and services. Our greatest strength is our global team - energetic, innovative people of all experience levels and talents who make GXO a great place to work. GXO is an equal opportunity employer. title: Depot Coordinator
description:
We're looking for a highly organised and proactive Depot Coordinator to support the smooth day-to-day running of our busy operation in Lutterworth. Acting as a key link between employees, managers, agency partners, and external suppliers, you'll provide essential administrative support that helps keep our site running efficiently.

This is a varied role offering exposure to people administration, payroll support, resource planning, reporting, employee engagement, and site coordination within a fast-paced logistics environment.

Apply today and become an integral part of our Wellingborough operation.

About the Role

As Depot Coordinator, you will:
- Support employee lifecycle administration, including onboarding, job changes, absence management, and leavers.
- Complete Right to Work checks and maintain accurate employee records.
- Record and monitor attendance, holidays, sickness, overtime, and worked hours using HR and Time & Attendance systems.
- Produce daily and weekly reports relating to staffing and operational performance.
- Liaise with agency providers to coordinate labour requirements.
- Support investigations, disciplinary meetings, and employee engagement activities through note-taking and administration.
- Manage reception and visitor processes, meeting room bookings, and site communications.
- Order and control office supplies and operational consumables.
- Support resource planning and general site administration activities.

Benefits
- 23 days' annual leave
- Company Pension
- Long service rewards: both financial and leave-based.
- Health cash plan.
- Life assurance scheme.
- Critical Illness cover
- Access to our prestige benefits and rewards portal.
- Career development opportunities.
- Access to a well-established Employee Assistance Programme provider.
- And other excellent benefits you'd expect from a market leader.

Requirements

Required Knowledge & Skills

What We're Looking For
- Previous experience in an administrative, depot, operations, HR, or logistics support role.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
- Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
- Confident communicator who can build relationships at all levels.
- Ability to handle confidential information professionally.
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
- Experience using HR, payroll, or Time & Attendance systems such as Kronos, UKG, HeRo, iTrent, or similar.
- GCSEs (or equivalent) and ideally a minimum of two years' experience in a similar role.

Additional Information
- 40 Hours per week, any 5 over 7 days
- This role supports a 24-hour operation, so flexibility around working hours may be required.
- Travel to other Whistl sites may occasionally be necessary.
- A driving licence and access to your own transport would be advantageous.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a supportive team where you can make a real impact on operational efficiency and employee experience.

title: Receptionist
description: Receptionist is responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and providing support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties may include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of personal information and assisting patients as required. To act as a central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with the multidisciplinary team member and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The core responsibilities of the receptionist are as follows. On occasion, there may be a requirement to carry out tasks not listed below, that are within the reasonable scope of the role. Maintain and monitor practice appointment system Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments Answer incoming phone calls, dealing with the callers request appropriately Signpost patients to the correct service Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as requested Input data as necessary onto patients healthcare records Direct requests for information to relevant team members i.e., SAR, DVLA forms, insurance/solicitors letters Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner Carry out system searches as requested Support all clinical staff with general tasks as required Photocopy documentation as required Maintain a clean, tidy and effective working area Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards In addition to the core responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to; 1. Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary 2. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the rota 3. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead 4. Support admin team, providing cover during absences 5. Scan patient related documents and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare record

title: Administrative Assistant
description: We are looking for a friendly, organised and reliable Administrative Assistant to join our team and provide essential administrative support to our reception team and the wider practice. This is a varied and rewarding role involving front-desk reception, telephone support, patient liaison and general administrative duties. You will be an important part of the practice team, helping to ensure the smooth and efficient running of our busy GP practice while providing a welcoming and professional service to our patients. The successful candidate will be a confident and approachable communicator who is able to build positive relationships with patients and colleagues. You will be well organised, able to prioritise and manage competing tasks effectively, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment. Flexibility is important, as you will be expected to work collaboratively across different areas of the practice and provide support to other teams when required. We are looking for someone who is proactive, adaptable and takes pride in delivering a high standard of service. This role is based across two practice sites, located approximately one mile apart. Hours of Work 26.25 hours per week , Monday to Friday Shift pattern includes both: AM shifts: 8.00am 1.15pm PM shifts: 1.15pm 6.30pm Over a two-week period, you will work 5 AM shifts and 5 PM shifts The successful candidate will provide professional front-desk and administrative support within the practice, assisting patients, managing appointments and enquiries, processing registrations and documentation, maintaining accurate records, and ensuring confidentiality. Support both clinical and non-clinical teams to help maintain the smooth and efficient running of the practice. Key Responsibilities Provide support to the reception team and wider practice. Welcome and assist patients at the front desk in a professional and friendly manner. Answer incoming telephone calls and deal with enquiries appropriately. Liaise with patients by telephone, in person and through other appropriate communication channels. Book, amend and manage patient appointments. Handle general administrative tasks and ensure work is completed accurately and efficiently. Process patient registrations and related documentation. Scan, upload and accurately file documents and correspondence. Deal with prescription enquiries and direct requests to the appropriate team where necessary. Manage emails and respond to or action enquiries appropriately. Provide administrative support to clinical and non-clinical teams when required. Maintain confidentiality and handle patient information in accordance with practice policies and procedures. Assist with maintaining accurate and up-to-date records. Support the smooth running of the reception and administrative functions. Undertake any other reasonable duties required to support the practice and its teams.

title: HR Administrator
description: Are you an experienced administrator with a passion for delivering excellent customer service and supporting people throughout their employment journey? We are looking for an organised and proactive HR Administrator to join our friendly and supportive HR Team. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in delivering a high-quality HR administration service across the organisation. As an HR Administrator, you will provide administrative support across a wide range of HR activities, including recruitment and onboarding, contractual changes, absence administration, mandatory training, HR systems administration and workforce reporting. You will work closely with managers, employees and colleagues across the organisation, providing a professional and responsive service while ensuring HR processes are completed accurately, efficiently and in line with organisational policies and procedures. This role would suit someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, has excellent attention to detail and takes pride in delivering a high standard of customer service. You will be joining a team where collaboration, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement are actively encouraged. Please note that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position. Applicants will be required to demonstrate their right to work in the UK at interview. Please note this is a part time role offering 30 hours per week. You will support the delivery of an efficient and effective HR administration service, acting as a first point of contact for routine HR enquiries and helping managers and employees navigate HR processes. You will support recruitment and onboarding activities, including advertising vacancies, undertaking pre-employment checks, preparing offer documentation and coordinating new starter processes. You will maintain accurate employee records and electronic personnel files, ensuring information is recorded securely and maintained in accordance with data protection requirements. You will also support the administration of key HR systems, including Bluestream, PCSA, Radar and RotaMaster. You will support sickness absence administration, maintaining accurate records, highlighting absence triggers and ensuring information is reported within required timescales. You will assist with mandatory training administration, professional registration monitoring and the production of HR reports and workforce data. Working closely with the wider HR Team, you will contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, support HR projects and help ensure a consistent, customer-focused service is delivered across the organisation. The HR Administrator will provide a high-quality, customer-focused HR administration service across the organisation, supporting the delivery of efficient, accurate and compliant HR processes.
